_meta.title: Mask Image (UGL-generated: white = regenerate, black = leave untouched)

Snap the cover to the nearest valid latent size AT ITS OWN ASPECT RATIO (UGL computes {{WORK_WIDTH}}/{{WORK_HEIGHT}} from the cover's real dimensions) — deliberately NOT the card's tall aspect ratio, or this stretch would distort the art. Card-shape reflow happens afterward in C#, not here.
Match mask to the working canvas size exactly
Convert mask image to a MASK
Load Flux.1 Fill Dev — switch weight_dtype to fp8_e4m3fn if you're short on VRAM
Differential Diffusion — Flux Fill's recommended technique for smoother blending at the mask edge

inputs.text: {{PROMPT}}, plain uncluttered box art background, matching colors and style, sharp detail, high resolution

_meta.title: CLIP Text Encode (Positive Prompt) — deliberately no negation ("no text"/"no logo"/etc.): diffusion models routinely render the very thing a prompt names even when told not to, and this workflow's cfg=1.0 (see KSampler) means the negative-prompt channel below is essentially inert, so there's no fallback path to suppress it either. Describe only the desired positive content.

Flux Guidance (10.0, lower than ComfyUI's official example's 30.0 — that example is a dramatic content-changing edit; ours wants the opposite, faithful continuation of the surrounding art, so less aggressive prompt-following is more appropriate here)
CLIP Text Encode (Negative) — left empty, matching ComfyUI's official Flux Fill example; Flux doesn't use classic negative-prompt CFG the way SD does, and KSampler's cfg is 1.0 below
Inpaint Model Conditioning — Flux Fill's own architecture handles mask-aware reconstruction here, unlike the old SD1.5 VAEEncodeForInpaint approach

KSampler (40 steps, up from ComfyUI's official example's 20 — testing showed text baked into a busy/gradient background region, unlike plain-background text, still came out garbled at 20 steps; cfg 1.0 is correct for Flux, guidance comes from the FluxGuidance node instead; denoise 1.0 is Flux Fill's own documented default, not a partial-denoise trick)
Paste the regenerated band back onto the ORIGINAL reflowed cover — Flux Fill already preserves unmasked content well on its own, but this guarantees it byte-for-byte regardless
Save Image — still at the cover's own aspect ratio, not the card's. UGL's ResizeCoverFit reflows this to the actual card size afterward, then composites the real logo on top.
